prompt:
A car of mass $1200\ \text{kg}$ accelerates from rest to $15\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ in $6.0\ \text{s}$.

**(a)** Calculate the average acceleration of the car. **[1]**

**(b)** Calculate the average resultant force on the car. **[1]**

**(c)** The driving force on the car is larger than your answer to (b). Explain why. **[1]**
markscheme:
**(a)** $a = \tfrac{15}{6.0} = 2.5\ \text{m s}^{-2}$ ✓

**(b)** $F = ma = 1200 \times 2.5 = 3.0 \times 10^3\ \text{N}$ ✓

**(c)** Resistive forces (air resistance, friction) act against the motion, so the driving force must exceed the resultant force by their size ✓
